_README.what: Cut points for every corpus file that was carved out of a FULL-VOLUME scan. Line numbers are 1-based and refer to the archive.org DjVuTXT of the whole volume named in `archive_item`, NOT to the corpus file (the corpus file additionally carries a 7-line provenance header: 5 comment lines, a blank line, and a ====== rule).
_README.not_listed_here: The 7 files taken from the Perm transcription (otlivka-1892-ch1..ch4, privilegiya-1891-*, doklad-irto-1895-*), the 2 patent PDFs, and the 2 ЭСБЕ wikisource articles are NOT full-volume scans — each of those URLs already resolves to exactly one document, so there is nothing to cut and no boundary to record.
_README.cross_cutting_finding: The single most fragile thing in this corpus is not the cut points but the OCR of the man's own name. Across the German volumes the same word comes out as `Slavianoff`, `Slawianoff`, `Slavianoff'sche`, `SlavianofF`, `Nicolai Slavianoff oiTimdene` and `SlavianofVche`; in Russian pre-reform type `Славяновъ` survives, but the surrounding column bleed splices neighbouring columns into the middle of sentences (see elektrichestvo-1892-0910, where two columns interleave from line ~532 onward). Every quotation pulled from these files must be re-read against the line range given here, not trusted from a grep.
